figures.finding: No permit or rule for a child performer appears: the Employment and Labour Relations Act 2025, Part II, forbids employing a child under fifteen, lets children of fifteen and over be employed with restrictions (light work, no hazardous or underground work, no night work, limited hours in industrial undertakings, rest days and public holidays), and its arrangement of sections names no exception for performing; so the general law reaches a child actor, writer or director as any employee (reading from the headings and the government's summary; the text itself is sold and wasn't read).

figures.finding: Botswana has no film fund to apply to: the Ministry of Sport and Arts commissions films directly, a National Film Commission awaits a Cinematography Act, and the National Arts Council announced in October 2026 a planned creative industry fund; so there is no applicant age to meet.

figures.finding: Botswana's age of majority is 18: Parliament lowered it from 21 in 2010 by amending the Interpretation Act, and from then a person has full legal capacity, contracting and suing without a guardian's assistance.
figures.applies: As the Government's memorandum to the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill states it in the Government Gazette of 10 July 2020 (No. 68); the Interpretation Act's amended text itself was not reached.
figures.webSearch: 2026-11-01: 'Botswana age of majority 18 years Act "Age of Majority" Botswana Cap 28:01' returned the Gazette of 10 July 2020 (used), the Government's Daily News (used), Mmegi, Citizenship Rights Africa.

sources.said: In 2010 Parliament amended the Interpretation Act by reducing the age of majority from 21 years to 18 years. The age of majority is a threshold of adulthood and a person who has attained the age of majority assumes full legal capacity and can, without assistance of his or her guardian, enter into a legally binding contract; sue and be sued in his or her own name, etc.
Parliament has amended the Citizenship Act of 2020 to align the legislation with the age of majority set out in the Interpretation Act.

figures.finding: Under the Children's Act 2009 a parent represents the child (under 18) in all contractual and other legal matters touching the child's property and interests; any employment of a child the Employment Act permits is for apprenticeship only, under a contract made with the written consent of a parent, other relative or guardian, and the employer files its records with the labour ministry. No set-aside of a child's earnings was found, and the Act draws no line between performing and other creative work.

figures.finding: Under the Companies Act (Cap. 42:01) a person under 18 may not be appointed or hold office as a company director; in a close company a minor member is represented by the guardian unless over 18 with the guardian's written consent lodged, wording that predates the 2010 lowering of majority to 18.

sources.said: 146. Qualifications of directors (1) A natural person who is not disqualified by subsection (2) of this section may be appointed as a director of a company. (2) The following persons are disqualified from being appointed or holding office as a director of a company ­ (a) a person who is under 18 years of age; ... (1) A minor who is a member of a close company, other than a minor over the age of 18 years whose guardian has lodged with the company a written consent to the minor's participation in the company, shall be represented in the close company by his guardian.
